title: slot-lane-reservoir: adaptive slot reservation and spill deferrer for KV cache
author: Elena Park
description:
Problem: under mixed tenant workloads we observed oscillatory spill behavior and long tail GC/compaction pauses when the KV cache hit a high fragmentation state. Existing slab and segment allocators used fixed reservation heuristics which either over-reserved space for noisy tenants or under-provisioned hot lanes, causing repeated spill waves that increased p99 latency and IO churn.

Proposal and approach: introduce a new 'slot-lane reservoir' allocator that separates cache residency into lightweight lanes per-tenant and a small shared reservoir. Key ideas: 1) lane reservations are elastic and decay over time based on access patterns (soft-threshold allocator), 2) a deferred spill controller (spill deferrer) batches spill operations and applies tenant-level pacing when downstream IO is saturated, 3) a compact-on-evict hook triggers opportunistic in-place compaction for highly fragmented lanes before spilling, and 4) metrics and trace points added to observe lane occupancy, reservoir pressure, and deferred-spill queue length. The design favors graceful degradation: when reservoir pressure rises we throttle low-priority lanes and avoid synchronized large spills via randomized jitter.

What this PR does: implements the slot-lane reservoir (pkg/kv/cache/reservoir.go, pkg/kv/allocator/slot_lane.go), adds unit and deterministic concurrency tests (pkg/kv/cache/reservoir_test.go), integrates a deferred-spill controller with tenant pacing (pkg/kv/spill/deferrer.go), exposes observability (metrics + span annotations), and updates the perf harness and Helm values for ramp testing.

Testing and benchmarks: microbenchmarks show a 35% reduction in spill events under synthetic mixed-tenancy load and a 22% improvement in p99 token-generation latency for latency-sensitive routes at 95th percentile reservoir pressure. CI includes unit tests, integration (small cluster) validation, and a benchmark job that ran twice to stabilize noisy results.

Upgrade/compat notes: no API changes. Configuration knobs are additive (reservoir_size, lane_decay_window_ms, spill_deferrer_max_batch) and default to off/low for safety. Operators can opt-in via Helm values or Redwood Console toggles.

Related work: follows ENG-1609 for fragmentation telemetry and ENG-1610 for spillback pacing heuristics.

Summary: this PR reduces noisy spill amplification and improves tail latency by combining elastic per-lane reservations with a deferred, paced spill controller and opportunistic compaction before eviction.
commits: 7 commits: 1) init slot-lane reservoir types and interfaces; 2) implement soft-threshold allocator and decay windows; 3) add deferred spill controller and tenant pacing; 4) integrate compact-on-evict hook; 5) add prometheus metrics and tracing annotations; 6) perf harness and helm defaults; 7) tests and flake fixes
changes_summary: Adds slot-lane reservoir allocator, deferred spill controller with tenant pacing, opportunistic compact-on-evict, and observability. Defaults are conservative; feature gated via config. Includes unit/integration tests and bench harness updates.
ci_checks: bench-stable: pass after rerun (bench noise reduced)
review_comments: Arjun: Please clarify how lane decay interacts with high-frequency bursts — recommend adding a bounded hysteresis to avoid thrashing.
Author (Elena): Added lane_decay_hysteresis in second commit and updated tests to cover burst scenarios.
Priya: Observability looks good but we should add an alert for deferred-spill queue length > 1000.
Author: Added alert rule and doc entry; default threshold set to 500 for cloud-managed clusters.
Samir: Minor nit: rename reservoir.pressure -> reservoir.utilization for clarity.
Author: Renamed and updated metrics export in commit 5.
benchmark_results: Under mixed workload (10 tenants, skewed hotset), spill count reduced from 1580 -> 1025 over 10 minutes; p99 latency for small-chat route reduced from 312ms -> 244ms. Bench harness details in bench/perf/kv_reservoir_bench.go.
test_plan: Unit tests cover allocator invariants, decay window, and deferred spill scheduling. Integration test deploys a 3-node small cluster and runs a mixed-tenancy synthetic driver for 15 minutes verifying no more than 2 sustained spill waves. Bench harness run for statistical significance (n=5).
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: new allocator paths could regress memory accounting and trigger unexpected OOMs in unusual cluster configurations. Mitigations: conservative default reservoir size, extensive unit tests, a feature gate and runtime flags to disable deferred spill controller, and extra prometheus metrics to detect anomalies quickly.
release_notes: Introduce slot-lane reservoir allocator to reduce spill amplification and improve tail latency under mixed-tenancy workloads. Add deferred spill controller with tenant pacing and compact-on-evict optimization. No user-facing API changes; configurable via Helm/Console.
notes: Deployed to canary cluster for 48h post-merge with telemetry indicating expected pressure behavior; plan to roll to wider fleet after 1 week of stability metrics.
